builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PARLEY: Evaluating LLM Collaboration Through Cooperative Asymmetric Puzzles
summary: PARLEY replaces ad hoc, single-metric evaluation of LLM agent pairs with a structured benchmark of asymmetric cooperative puzzles plus the PAC failure taxonomy (Perception, Adaptation, Coordination) for diagnosing collaboration breakdowns. It costs an evaluation harness and API inference spend for conversation rollouts, and the intervention adds taxonomy-derived guidance to agent prompts rather than model changes. Findings may not transfer: results come from GPT-4o pairs on four puzzle tasks, so failure categories and the 10-point gain may shift with different models, domains, or real production tasks.
rationale: The failure taxonomy and feedback-integration checks are cheap to adapt for debugging multi-agent pipelines, but the reported gains are puzzle-benchmark specific and must be validated on the reader's own agent workload before adoption.

claims.statement: PARLEY replaces ad hoc, single-metric evaluation of LLM agent pairs with a structured benchmark of asymmetric cooperative puzzles plus the PAC failure taxonomy (Perception, Adaptation, Coordination) for diagnosing collaboration breakdowns. It costs an evaluation harness and API inference spend for conversation rollouts, and the intervention adds taxonomy-derived guidance to agent prompts rather than model changes. Findings may not transfer: results come from GPT-4o pairs on four puzzle tasks, so failure categories and the 10-point gain may shift with different models, domains, or real production tasks.
GPT-4o agent pairs achieved 60.5% task success (N=400); a taxonomy-guided intervention raised average success to 70.5% (N=200), a 10-point absolute improvement, not a multiplicative factor.
